title: Saying No to a Close Friend
situation: A close friend asks to borrow a significant amount of money. You can technically afford it, but you do not feel comfortable giving it.

questions.label: WHAT IS MAKING THIS HARD?
questions.prompt: What is the strongest reason you are hesitating to say no?
options: I am afraid they will think I do not care about them.
I feel guilty because I could afford to help.
I worry this could damage our friendship.
I do not know how to explain my refusal.
I am not completely sure I want to refuse.

questions.label: NAME THE REAL CONCERN
questions.prompt: If money were removed from the situation, what would you still be worried about?
questions.placeholder: “Without the money part, I would still worry that…”

questions.label: SEPARATE CARE FROM OBLIGATION
questions.prompt: Finish each sentence in your own words.
fields: Helping my friend would feel right because…
Helping my friend would feel wrong because…
What I actually owe this person is…

questions.label: REVERSE THE SITUATION
questions.prompt: If you were asking a friend for the same amount and they calmly said no, what would you consider reasonable?
options: I would be disappointed, but I would respect it.
I would probably take it personally.
It would depend on how they explained it.

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: After thinking through the friendship, your boundaries, and your responsibility, what do you want to do?
questions.placeholder: “My decision is… The main reason is… I want to communicate it by…”

title: A Better Job in Another City
situation: You receive a job offer in another city. The salary is noticeably better, but accepting it means leaving your current environment, routines, and people behind.

questions.label: FIRST REACTION
questions.prompt: What did you feel first when you imagined accepting the offer?

questions.label: WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CHANGE?
questions.prompt: WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CHANGE?
fields: Three things I would gain:
Three things I would lose:
One thing I might be exaggerating:

questions.label: WHAT IS PULLING YOU MOST?
questions.prompt: If salary were identical in both jobs, what would matter most?

questions.label: FEAR OR SIGNAL?
questions.prompt: What exactly are you afraid might happen if you move?

questions.label: TEST THE OPPOSITE
questions.prompt: Now imagine you reject the offer. What might you regret six months from now?

questions.label: ADVICE FROM DISTANCE
questions.prompt: ADVICE FROM DISTANCE
fields: If my best friend were in this situation, I would tell them…
The part of that advice I find hardest to follow myself is…

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What currently feels like the more honest choice, and what information do you still need before deciding?
questions.placeholder: “Right now I am leaning toward… Before deciding, I still need to know…”

title: Staying in a Relationship That Feels Different
situation: Nothing dramatic has happened, but your relationship no longer feels the way it used to. You are unsure whether this is a temporary phase or a sign that something important has changed.

questions.label: WHAT CHANGED FIRST?
questions.prompt: Which change feels most noticeable?
options: I feel less excited to spend time together.
I cannot identify one specific change.

questions.label: FACTS VS INTERPRETATIONS
questions.prompt: FACTS VS INTERPRETATIONS
fields: What has objectively changed?
What am I assuming those changes mean?

questions.label: REMOVE THE HISTORY
questions.prompt: If you met this person today, knowing only how the relationship feels right now, what would you think?

questions.label: WHAT ARE YOU PROTECTING?
questions.prompt: What would be hardest to lose?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What conversation, action, or boundary would give you more clarity before making a bigger decision?
questions.placeholder: “Before deciding anything major, I want to…”

title: Buying Something Expensive You Really Want
situation: You want to buy something expensive. You can pay for it without going into debt, but the purchase would significantly reduce your savings.

questions.label: WHAT ARE YOU BUYING?
questions.prompt: What does this purchase represent to you most?

questions.label: THE WEEK-AFTER TEST
questions.prompt: Imagine you bought it seven days ago. What would make you feel satisfied with the decision?
questions.placeholder: “I would feel it was worth it if…”

questions.label: COMPARE THE TWO COSTS
questions.prompt: COMPARE THE TWO COSTS
fields: What do I gain by buying it now?
What do I give up by spending this money now?
What happens if I wait 30 days?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What condition would make this purchase feel like a clear yes or a clear no?
questions.placeholder: “I will buy it if… I will wait if…”

title: A Colleague Takes Credit for Your Work
situation: During a meeting, a colleague presents an idea you developed together in a way that makes it sound like it was primarily theirs.

questions.label: YOUR FIRST IMPULSE
questions.prompt: What do you most want to do?
options: Wait and see if it happens again.

questions.label: DEFINE THE PROBLEM
questions.prompt: What exactly bothered you: the loss of recognition, the unfairness, the possible career impact, or something else?

questions.label: THREE POSSIBLE EXPLANATIONS
questions.prompt: Write three explanations for what happened, including at least one that is less negative than your first interpretation.
fields: Explanation 1:
Explanation 2:
Explanation 3:

questions.label: WHAT RESULT DO YOU WANT?
questions.prompt: Which outcome matters most?

questions.label: SAY IT WITHOUT ATTACKING
questions.prompt: Write one sentence you could actually say to your colleague.
questions.placeholder: “I wanted to clarify something about today’s meeting…”

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What action gives you the best chance of protecting both your contribution and the working relationship?

title: A Friend Keeps Canceling Plans
situation: A friend has canceled plans with you several times at the last minute. They always apologize, but you are starting to feel that your time is not being respected.

questions.label: WHAT HURTS MOST?
questions.prompt: WHAT HURTS MOST?
options: Not knowing whether I can rely on them
Feeling foolish for continuing to make plans

questions.label: LOOK AT THE PATTERN
questions.prompt: LOOK AT THE PATTERN
fields: What has happened repeatedly?
What explanation have they given?
What have I never clearly told them?

questions.label: CHOOSE THE BOUNDARY
questions.prompt: Which response feels most reasonable?
options: Tell them directly how it affects me.
Only make flexible plans with them.
Accept that this is simply how they are.

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What boundary would protect your time without turning the situation into unnecessary conflict?

title: You Want to Quit Something You Recently Started
situation: You started a course, project, hobby, or new routine with enthusiasm. A few weeks later, you feel like quitting.

questions.label: WHY DO YOU WANT TO STOP?
questions.prompt: WHY DO YOU WANT TO STOP?
options: I do not have enough time.
I started for the wrong reason.

questions.label: REMEMBER THE BEGINNING
questions.prompt: Why did you start in the first place?

questions.label: QUITTING VS ADJUSTING
questions.prompt: QUITTING VS ADJUSTING
fields: What would happen if I quit completely?
What would happen if I reduced the commitment instead?
What is the smallest version I could continue?

questions.label: HONEST CHECK
questions.prompt: Which statement feels closest to the truth?
options: I genuinely do not want this anymore.
I want the result but dislike the difficult middle.
I am overloaded and need to reduce the pace.
I am afraid I will fail.

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Are you quitting, pausing, reducing the commitment, or continuing? Explain why.

title: Someone Offers You an Opportunity You Did Not Ask For
situation: You are unexpectedly offered an opportunity that could change your direction: a new role, partnership, trip, project, or responsibility. It sounds exciting, but it was never part of your plan.

questions.label: WHAT ATTRACTS YOU?
questions.prompt: WHAT ATTRACTS YOU?
options: Simply the fact that it is new

questions.label: WHAT MAKES YOU HESITATE?
questions.prompt: WHAT MAKES YOU HESITATE?
options: I would need to change existing plans.
I am unsure whether I truly want it.
It could take too much time.
I am afraid of saying yes for the wrong reason.

questions.label: OPPORTUNITY OR DISTRACTION?
questions.prompt: OPPORTUNITY OR DISTRACTION?
fields: How does this support the direction I already want?
How could this pull me away from that direction?
What part is exciting mainly because someone chose me?

questions.label: REMOVE THE EGO
questions.prompt: If nobody else ever knew you received this opportunity, would you still want it?

questions.label: THE PRICE OF YES
questions.prompt: What would you have to stop, delay, or give less attention to if you accepted?

questions.label: WHICH LOSS FEELS WORSE?
questions.prompt: WHICH LOSS FEELS WORSE?
options: Disappointing the person who offered it

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Is this opportunity aligned with your direction, or is it simply difficult to refuse?
questions.placeholder: “I am leaning toward… because… The trade-off I am accepting is…”

title: You Disagree With Your Partner About a Major Purchase
situation: You want to spend money on something important to you, while your partner believes the money should be saved or used for another priority.

questions.label: WHAT IS THIS REALLY ABOUT?
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THIS REALLY ABOUT?

questions.label: DEFINE BOTH SIDES
questions.prompt: DEFINE BOTH SIDES
fields: My strongest argument is…
Their strongest argument is…
The part of their argument I actually agree with is…

questions.label: FIND THE VALUE UNDERNEATH
questions.prompt: What value are you trying to protect with your position?
questions.placeholder: “Freedom / security / enjoyment / fairness / progress / something else…”

questions.label: BUILD A THIRD OPTION
questions.prompt: What compromise is different from both “buy it” and “do not buy it”?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What outcome would feel fair even if neither person gets exactly what they originally wanted?

title: You Are Thinking About Ending a Long Friendship
situation: A friendship that once felt important now regularly leaves you drained, frustrated, or uncomfortable. You are wondering whether to distance yourself.

questions.label: WHAT HAS CHANGED?
questions.prompt: WHAT HAS CHANGED?
fields: What used to make this friendship valuable?
What feels different now?
When did I first notice the change?

questions.label: PATTERN OR PHASE?
questions.prompt: How does the problem feel?
options: Something caused by one unresolved conflict
A change in who we both are

questions.label: WHAT HAVE YOU TRIED?
questions.prompt: What have you already done to improve the situation?

questions.label: IMAGINE NOTHING CHANGES
questions.prompt: If the friendship stayed exactly like this for another year, how would you feel?
options: Relieved if we naturally grew apart

questions.label: TWO KINDS OF LOSS
questions.prompt: TWO KINDS OF LOSS
fields: What would I lose by stepping away?
What would I regain by stepping away?

questions.label: ONE HONEST CONVERSATION
questions.prompt: If you knew the friendship could survive honesty, what would you finally say?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What feels more appropriate now: repairing the friendship, changing its boundaries, creating distance, or ending it?
questions.placeholder: “I think the next step should be… because…”

title: Turning Down a Promotion
situation: You are offered a promotion with more money and status, but the new role would include responsibilities you are not sure you actually want.

questions.label: WHAT ATTRACTS YOU MOST?
questions.prompt: What makes the promotion appealing?
options: I genuinely want the new work

questions.label: WANT OR EXPECTATION?
questions.prompt: How much do you personally want this role, separate from what others may expect from you?
scaleLabels: 1 — I mostly feel I should want it

questions.label: COMPARE THE REAL JOB
questions.prompt: COMPARE THE REAL JOB
fields: What would I enjoy more in the new role?
What would I miss from my current role?
What new responsibility worries me most?

questions.label: REMOVE THE TITLE
questions.prompt: If the title and salary stayed the same, would you still want the responsibilities?

questions.label: THE COST OF ACCEPTING
questions.prompt: What would this promotion require from you outside the job description?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Do you want the promotion itself, or mainly what the promotion represents?

title: Moving Back Closer to Family
situation: You live far from your family and have built a life elsewhere. You are considering moving closer, but doing so could change your career, independence, and daily routine.

questions.label: WHAT IS PULLING YOU BACK?
questions.prompt: WHAT IS PULLING YOU BACK?
options: I feel guilty being far away.
I want a slower or more familiar life.
I no longer feel connected to where I live now.

questions.label: TWO VERSIONS OF HOME
questions.prompt: TWO VERSIONS OF HOME
fields: What does my current life give me?
What would living near family give me?
What does neither option solve?

questions.label: WHAT MATTERS MOST?
questions.prompt: Rank these from most important to least important.

questions.label: GUILT CHECK
questions.prompt: If nobody felt disappointed by your decision, where would you genuinely prefer to live?

questions.label: MAKE IT REVERSIBLE
questions.prompt: Is there a smaller experiment you could try before making a permanent move?

questions.label: WHICH REGRET FEELS HEAVIER?
questions.prompt: WHICH REGRET FEELS HEAVIER?
options: Giving up the life I built
Making the move and wanting to leave again

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What decision best reflects what you value now, not what you valued several years ago?

title: Lending Your Car to Someone You Do Not Fully Trust
situation: Someone close to you asks to borrow your car. You want to help, but you do not fully trust how careful they are.

questions.label: WHAT IS THE REAL RISK?
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE REAL RISK?

questions.label: SAY THE UNSPOKEN PART
questions.prompt: What are you afraid to tell them directly?

questions.label: FIND OTHER WAYS TO HELP
questions.prompt: FIND OTHER WAYS TO HELP
fields: Instead of lending the car, I could…
A reasonable boundary would be…

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What response lets you help without ignoring your own discomfort?

title: Posting Something Personal Online
situation: You want to share something personal online. Part of you wants to be open, while another part wonders whether you may regret making it public.

questions.label: WHY DO YOU WANT TO POST IT?
questions.prompt: WHY DO YOU WANT TO POST IT?
options: To get a specific person's attention

questions.label: WHO ARE YOU ACTUALLY TALKING TO?
questions.prompt: Select all that apply.

questions.label: TOMORROW MORNING TEST
questions.prompt: How would you feel if you woke up tomorrow and knew everyone had seen it?

questions.label: WHAT IF THERE WERE NO REACTIONS?
questions.prompt: Would you still want to post it if nobody could like, comment, or respond?

questions.label: THREE OPTIONS
questions.prompt: THREE OPTIONS
fields: What happens if I post it now?
What happens if I wait 24 hours?
What happens if I share it privately instead?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Is sharing this helping you express something important, or are you hoping the audience will change how you feel?

title: Giving Someone a Second Chance
situation: Someone who disappointed or hurt you asks for another chance. You still care about them, but you are not sure whether trusting them again is wise.

questions.label: WHAT HAPPENED?
questions.prompt: Which description fits best?

questions.label: APOLOGY VS CHANGE
questions.prompt: APOLOGY VS CHANGE
fields: What have they said?
What have they actually done differently?
What would real change look like to me?

questions.label: CURRENT TRUST
questions.prompt: How much trust is actually present right now?

questions.label: DEFINE A SECOND CHANCE
questions.prompt: What would giving another chance mean in practice?
questions.placeholder: “It would mean I am willing to…, but not willing to…”

questions.label: WHAT ARE YOU AFRAID OF?
questions.prompt: WHAT ARE YOU AFRAID OF?

questions.label: CONDITIONS, NOT PROMISES
questions.prompt: What would need to happen for trust to rebuild gradually?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Are you ready to reopen trust, keep distance, or wait for more evidence?

title: Choosing Between Two Good Opportunities
situation: You have two genuinely good options, and choosing one means giving up the other.

questions.label: NAME THE OPTIONS
questions.prompt: NAME THE OPTIONS
fields: Option A:
Option B:

questions.label: YOUR DECISION CRITERIA
questions.prompt: Rank what matters most.

questions.label: BEST CASE
questions.prompt: BEST CASE
fields: Best realistic outcome of Option A:
Best realistic outcome of Option B:

questions.label: WORST CASE
questions.prompt: WORST CASE
fields: Worst realistic outcome of Option A:
Worst realistic outcome of Option B:

questions.label: WHICH OPTION NEEDS MORE EXPLAINING?
questions.prompt: Which choice do you feel you would need to justify more to other people?

questions.label: REMOVE OTHER PEOPLE
questions.prompt: If nobody could judge your choice, which option would you choose?

questions.label: INNER PULL
questions.prompt: Where are you leaning right now?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Which trade-off are you more willing to live with?

title: Someone Keeps Asking for Advice but Never Takes It
situation: Someone regularly comes to you with the same problem, asks for advice, ignores it, then returns with the same issue again.

questions.label: HOW DO YOU FEEL?
questions.prompt: HOW DO YOU FEEL?

questions.label: WHAT ROLE ARE YOU PLAYING?
questions.prompt: What do you think they actually want from you: advice, reassurance, permission, attention, or simply someone to listen?

questions.label: CHANGE YOUR RESPONSE
questions.prompt: CHANGE YOUR RESPONSE
fields: What do I usually do?
What could I do differently next time?

questions.label: WHAT BOUNDARY FITS?
questions.prompt: WHAT BOUNDARY FITS?
options: Ask what they want from the conversation first.
Tell them I cannot keep discussing the same issue.
Keep helping as I do now.
Reduce how available I am for this topic.

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: How can you care about this person without taking responsibility for their choices?

title: Keeping a Secret That Affects Someone Else
situation: Someone trusted you with private information, but you now realize that keeping the secret may negatively affect another person.

questions.label: WHAT ARE YOU PROTECTING?
questions.prompt: WHAT ARE YOU PROTECTING?
options: My own relationship with both people

questions.label: WHO IS AFFECTED?
questions.prompt: WHO IS AFFECTED?
fields: Who could be harmed if I stay silent?
Who could be harmed if I speak?
How serious is each possible harm?

questions.label: IS IT YOUR INFORMATION TO SHARE?
questions.prompt: IS IT YOUR INFORMATION TO SHARE?

questions.label: LOOK FOR A THIRD OPTION
questions.prompt: Is there a way to encourage the person to address the issue themselves before you intervene?

questions.label: DRAW THE LINE
questions.prompt: What would make staying silent no longer acceptable to you?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What action best balances privacy, trust, and responsibility?

title: Going Back to a Previous Job
situation: A previous employer asks whether you would consider returning. You left for a reason, but the new offer is attractive.

questions.label: REMEMBER WHY YOU LEFT
questions.prompt: REMEMBER WHY YOU LEFT
fields: The main reason I left was…
What has actually changed since then?
What might still be exactly the same?

questions.label: WHAT IS ATTRACTING YOU BACK?
questions.prompt: WHAT IS ATTRACTING YOU BACK?
options: Dissatisfaction with where I am now

questions.label: DO NOT COMPARE TO A BAD WEEK
questions.prompt: If your current situation suddenly improved, would the old job still seem attractive?

questions.label: IS THE ORIGINAL PROBLEM SOLVED?
questions.prompt: IS THE ORIGINAL PROBLEM SOLVED?
options: I do not have enough information

questions.label: QUESTIONS BEFORE YES
questions.prompt: Write three things you need clarified before making a decision.
fields: I need to know…
I need to know…
I need to know…

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Are you being pulled toward a better opportunity, or simply toward something familiar?

title: Canceling Plans Because You Need Time Alone
situation: You agreed to meet people, but now the day has arrived and you feel emotionally or mentally drained. You want to cancel, but you feel guilty.

questions.label: WHY DO YOU WANT TO CANCEL?
questions.prompt: WHY DO YOU WANT TO CANCEL?
options: I simply do not feel like it.
I often cancel when the time comes.

questions.label: ENERGY CHECK
questions.prompt: How much energy do you realistically have for the plan?

questions.label: PATTERN CHECK
questions.prompt: Is this an exception, or do you often want connection when making plans and isolation when the day arrives?

questions.label: WHAT WOULD HELP MOST?
questions.prompt: WHAT WOULD HELP MOST?
options: Push myself to go as planned.

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What choice respects both your current capacity and the other person's time?

title: Sharing Honest Feedback That May Hurt Someone
situation: Someone asks for your honest opinion about something important to them. You believe the truth may disappoint or hurt them.

questions.label: WHAT ARE THEY REALLY ASKING FOR?
questions.prompt: WHAT ARE THEY REALLY ASKING FOR?

questions.label: TRUTH VS DELIVERY
questions.prompt: TRUTH VS DELIVERY
fields: What do I genuinely think?
What part is useful for them to hear?
What part would only be unnecessarily harsh?

questions.label: SAY IT WITH CARE
questions.prompt: Write the most honest version you could say without trying to embarrass or diminish them.

questions.label: IS NOW THE RIGHT TIME?
questions.prompt: IS NOW THE RIGHT TIME?
options: No, they are too emotionally involved right now

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: What combination of honesty and care would actually help this person?

title: Spending More to Save Time
situation: You can pay more for a service or convenience that would save you several hours each week.

questions.label: WHY ARE YOU HESITATING?
questions.prompt: WHY ARE YOU HESITATING?
options: I am worried about forming an expensive habit.
I am unsure whether the saved time is really valuable.
The price is genuinely high for my budget.

questions.label: MAKE THE TRADE VISIBLE
questions.prompt: MAKE THE TRADE VISIBLE
fields: Extra monthly cost:
Hours saved per month:

questions.label: WHAT WOULD HAPPEN TO THE TIME?
questions.prompt: WHAT WOULD HAPPEN TO THE TIME?
fields: The saved time would probably go toward…
The money would otherwise go toward…

questions.label: IF IT WERE FREE
questions.prompt: Would you immediately choose the time-saving option if cost were removed?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: In this case, is your money more valuable to you than the time you would recover?

title: Agreeing to Something Because Everyone Else Is Doing It
situation: Your friends, colleagues, or peers are excited about doing something together, but you are not sure you actually want to join.

questions.label: FIRST HONEST ANSWER
questions.prompt: If nobody else were doing it, would you still want to?

questions.label: WHAT IS INFLUENCING YOU?
questions.prompt: WHAT IS INFLUENCING YOU?

questions.label: WHAT WOULD NO COST?
questions.prompt: What do you think might happen socially if you say no?

questions.label: REALISTIC CHECK
questions.prompt: How likely is that consequence actually to happen?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Are you choosing the experience itself, or choosing not to feel left out?

title: Waiting for Someone to Change
situation: You care about someone, but an important part of the relationship depends on them changing a behavior they have promised to change before.

questions.label: PROMISES AND PATTERNS
questions.prompt: PROMISES AND PATTERNS
fields: What have they promised?
What has actually changed?
How long have I been waiting?

questions.label: WHAT KEEPS YOU HOPEFUL?
questions.prompt: WHAT KEEPS YOU HOPEFUL?

questions.label: ACCEPT TODAY'S VERSION
questions.prompt: If this person never changed this behavior, could you accept the relationship as it is now?

questions.label: REALITY VS POTENTIAL
questions.prompt: How much of your decision is based on who they are today versus who you believe they could become?

questions.label: DEFINE CHANGE
questions.prompt: DEFINE CHANGE
fields: A meaningful sign of change would be…
A temporary improvement would look like…

questions.label: SET A BOUNDARY
questions.prompt: What do you need to stop waiting indefinitely?

questions.label: YOUR CONCLUSION
questions.prompt: Are you choosing this relationship as it exists today, or mainly choosing hope for a different version of it?
